description: Composite two-panel figure, both panels grouped bar charts sharing one colour legend (0.59 Si red, 1.07 Si blue, 1.56 Si green) and the same eleven x-axis categories: Al Mn S O, AlN, Al-N-Mn-O, Al-N-Mn-S, Mn-Al-O, MnO, MnS, Other oxides, Other oxi-sulfides, Other sulfides, Micro-defects. (a) plots inclusion density with y-axis "Particles/mm²" from 0 to 80 in 10-unit gridlines; the dominant bar is Micro-defects for 0.59 Si, rising to just below the 80 gridline, while the 1.56 Si bar is at roughly half that height and 1.07 Si is lower still. MnS, Al-N-Mn-O and AlN are the next most populated categories (all within the tens), and every remaining inclusion type stays in the low single digits. (b) plots "Average size, microns" from 0 to 4 in 0.5-unit gridlines for the same categories; most bars lie between about 1 and 3 microns, the tallest being MnO for 1.07 Si (above the 3 gridline) and Al Mn S O for 0.59 Si (near 3 micron), with no clear systematic difference between the three steels. Together the panels argue that inclusion number and size are comparable across the three silicon-containing steels and that only micro-defects/porosity clearly separates the 0.59 Si steel. No data labels are printed; values are read only against the gridlines.

observations.observation: Both panels are grouped bar charts sharing one legend with three colour-coded steels: 0.59 Si, 1.07 Si and 1.56 Si.
Panel (a) y-axis is labelled 'Particles/mm²' with gridlines at 0 to 80 in steps of 10.
Panel (b) y-axis is labelled 'Average size, microns' with gridlines at 0 to 4 in steps of 0.5.
Both panels use the identical x-axis category set: Al Mn S O, AlN, Al-N-Mn-O, Al-N-Mn-S, Mn-Al-O, MnO, MnS, Other oxides, Other oxi-sulfides, Other sulfides and Micro-defects.
In panel (a) the Micro-defects category is by far the largest; the 0.59 Si bar rises to just below the 80 particles/mm² gridline, more than twice the 1.07 Si bar and above the 1.56 Si bar.
In panel (a) the remaining populated categories are MnS, Al-N-Mn-O and AlN, whose bars reach the tens of particles/mm², while all other inclusion types remain in the low single digits.

In panel (b) the average inclusion sizes are broadly similar between the three steels, with most bars between about 1 and 3 microns and the tallest MnO bar (1.07 Si) standing above the 3 micron gridline.
No numeric data labels are printed on the bars in either panel; values can only be read relative to the gridlines.
The caption states that the number of inclusions is very similar between the silicon-containing steels and that the only difference is the much larger amount of porosity in the 0.59% Si steel.
The caption states that the average inclusion size was largely similar between the different steels (panel b).
The citing text states the total inclusion density was similar between the three low-phosphorus silicon-containing steels, between 62 and 78 inclusions/mm².
The citing text states the porosity in the 0.59% Si steel was more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel.
The citing text attributes the lowered toughness of the aged 0.59% Si sample to its increased amount of porosity, linking this figure to the toughness discussion.

The caption describes the panel (a) difference as 'porosity', whereas the plotted x-axis category carrying that difference is labelled 'Micro-defects'; the two are not explicitly linked in the figure itself.
Inclusion analysis for these steels was performed using an automated feature analysis according to the citing text.

subfigures.description: Grouped bar chart of inclusion density by inclusion type; y-axis 'Particles/mm²' 0-80 with 10-unit gridlines, x-axis listing eleven inclusion categories. Bars coloured by steel: 0.59 Si (red), 1.07 Si (blue), 1.56 Si (green). The Micro-defects bars dominate, the 0.59 Si bar reaching just below 80 particles/mm², with 1.56 Si about half of that and 1.07 Si the lowest; MnS, Al-N-Mn-O and AlN follow, all others low.

Grouped bar chart of average inclusion size for the same eleven inclusion categories and same three steels; y-axis 'Average size, microns' 0-4 with 0.5-unit gridlines. Most bars fall between roughly 1 and 3 microns; MnO for 1.07 Si is the tallest (above 3 microns) and Al Mn S O for 0.59 Si is near 3 microns. Sizes are broadly similar between the three steels.

unreadable_items: No data labels on bars in either panel; individual bar values are only estimable relative to gridlines, not read exactly
Small bars in panel (a) for 'Other oxides', 'Other oxi-sulfides' and 'Other sulfides' are of very low height and cannot be distinguished precisely between the three steels in panel (b)
